prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively name a single “best” roofer for all Dallas homes — the right contractor depends on your location in Dallas, budget, roof type, whether the job is storm/insurance-related, and how important things like long warranties or premium materials are to you. I can, however, help you find the best contractor for your situation and give a checklist to vet candidates.

Quick next step
- Tell me your ZIP code (or neighborhood) and what matters most (lowest price, best warranty, speed, insurance-claim experience, premium materials, etc.). I’ll suggest 3–5 well‑rated local roofers and a prioritized list of questions to ask them.

How to pick the best roofer (checklist)
1. Licensing & insurance
   - Confirm the company is licensed (if required) and carries general liability and workers’ comp insurance. Ask for certificates and verify they’re current.
2. Local experience and reputation
   - Prefer roofers with several years serving Dallas and good Google/Angi/Yelp/BBB reviews. Ask for 3 recent references with similar work.
3. Written estimate & scope
   - Get at least 3 detailed, written quotes that list materials (brand & model), removal vs overlay, tear-off disposal, decking repairs, permits, and timeline.
4. Warranties
   - Distinguish manufacturer shingle warranties from contractor workmanship warranties. Ask how long each covers and whether warranties are transferable.
5. Materials & quality
   - Verify the exact shingle line (manufacturer and class), underlayment, flashing, drip edge, vents, and chimney/valley treatments.
6. Insurance & storm experience (if applicable)
   - If filing a homeowner’s insurance claim, choose a roofer experienced with insurance adjusters and documentation; avoid firms that pressure you to sign over checks.
7. Permits & cleanup
   - Contractor should pull required permits, provide inspection documentation, and include jobsite cleanup and magnet sweep.
8. Payment terms
   - Beware of large upfront cash-only payments. Typical schedules are small deposit, progress payment, final payment after inspection.
9. Safety & subcontractors
   - Ask whether they use their own crews or subcontract; confirm site safety practices.
10. Red flags
   - High-pressure sales, only accepting cash, no written contract, very low bids that seem too good to be true, poor communication, no local references.

Typical cost ranges (ballpark)
- Dallas: full asphalt shingle roof replacement for an average-size single-family home commonly runs roughly $5,000–$20,000 depending on roof square footage, pitch/complexity, number of layers removed, and shingle grade. Premium materials (metal, tile, architectural shingles) cost more. Get three local bids to narrow actual cost for your roof.

Sample questions to ask a roofer
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide certificates?
- Who will perform the work — your employees or subs?
- Will you pull permits and arrange inspections?
- What exactly is included in the written estimate?
- What brand and warranty of shingles do you use? Is the workmanship warranty written?
- How do you protect landscaping and gutters? How is debris removed?
- Can you provide 3 recent local references and before/after photos?
- How do you handle any insurance claims (if applicable)?

If you want, provide your ZIP code and priorities and I’ll list 3–5 highly rated Dallas roofers to consider and draft an email/template you can send to them for consistent quotes.
